assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. One perfectly regular 3-column by 3-row atlas of NINE separate original picture tiles for a first-grade Chinese classroom about a community winter exhibit. Square canvas, strong ivory gutters centered at the exact thirds, independent square scenes with quiet light margins. Consistent matte gouache and cut-paper silhouettes, fine paper grain, deep pine, warm cream, apricot, persimmon and sky teal. Large instantly readable subjects, never any text, letters, numerals, characters, signs, labels, watermarks or textbook artwork. Row one from left: (1) autumn courtyard with a ginkgo branch and many ochre leaves visibly lifted into a curved gust, one trunk, empty of people; (2) early-spring apricot tree with open pink blossoms and a few petals lifting diagonally from a branch, bright spring green surroundings and no autumn leaves; (3) choppy broad blue river with distinct rolling crest lines and whitecaps seen from a quiet shore, no boat. Row two: (4) green bamboo grove with many distinct tall culms bowed diagonally to the RIGHT in the same gust, bamboo leaves only, no buildings; (5) close-up of a child hand holding freshly peeled tangerine with curling orange rind set apart clearly on an ivory plate; (6) close-up of rough layered dark brown pine bark still attached to a standing trunk, with a small hand softly touching the rough surface, no fruit. Row three: (7) a young East Asian girl with black bob and cream persimmon coat stepping back INTO an original pine-green arched doorway, body facing inside, about to meet a waiting adult; (8) a smiling child with one hand raised and mouth speaking an answer to a kind teacher in a plain classroom corner, no writing on walls; (9) an empty quiet community exhibition counter with soft lantern, folded paper flags and a single plain wooden box to one side, no people or shelves in foreground. Every image contains its whole intended central subject within its own cell. All pictures use one approachable style and clear differences in action. Avoid ornate details or thin outlines.
